text.p: European gains pushed Portuguese futures higher while cash bonds retreated after their strong rise on Tuesday to trade narrowly in a market devoid of liquidity before the May Day holiday.

Dealers said the cash market was waiting for further U.S. indicators later today but was unlikely to perk up before tomorrow's market holiday which will probably mean a long weekend for many investors.
Three-year bonds saw some profit-taking following recent gains but traders said the impact of this had been exaggerated by thin volume and support remained.
Dealers said fading hopes that the Bank of Portugal would cut rates on Friday when it sets conditions for the next commercial bank cash reserves period might also be behind the light selling.
All 10 analysts in a poll conducted by Reuters said the central bank would keep its key rates unchanged.
They thought that the Bank had room to cut rates but would probably wait until after April consumer price inflation data which is due by the middle of next month.
